title: Questioning the Survey Responses of Large Language Models

paper.authors: Ricardo Dominguez-Olmedo, Moritz Hardt, Celestine Mendler-Duenner
paper.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (NeurIPS 2024)

dependence.note: The paper characterises the answer distributions of 43 language models (next-token probabilities over choice letters); the OpenAI arms are text-davinci-001/002/003, gpt-3.5-turbo-0613, gpt-4-0613 and 'GPT-4 Turbo 0125' (= gpt-4-turbo-preview / gpt-4-0125-preview). All original responses are downloadable (results.zip, 4.48 GB, keeper.mpdl.mpg.de share).

claim.statement: Instruction-tuned OpenAI models, including GPT-4 Turbo 0125, exhibit substantial A-bias (systematic preference for the first answer label) on the 25 ACS questions (Figure 3), and after adjusting for choice ordering their answer distributions remain much closer to a uniform baseline than to the U.S. census or any state subgroup (Figures 4-5); even for 'the GPT-4 model' with the highest similarity to human reference populations only 6 of 25 questions (24%) are closer to the U.S. census than to uniform (Section 4.2).
claim.metric: A-bias_q = P(adjusted response = 'A') - 1/k_q (Eq. 1); normalized entropy of adjusted responses; mean KL(model || census) vs mean KL(model || uniform) over 25 ACS questions

original_values.gpt4_questions_closer_to_census_than_uni: 6/25 (24%) - text says 'the GPT-4 model', ambiguous between gpt-4-0613 and gpt-4-0125-preview
original_values.per_model_A_bias_entropy_KL: figure-level only (Figures 3, 4, 5); numeric values must be extracted from results.zip (4,476,107,528 bytes) via figures.ipynb
original_values.note: No table reports the GPT-4 Turbo 0125 numbers in the paper text.

claim.original_source: Figures 3-5 and Section 4.2 of arXiv 2306.07951 (NeurIPS 2024 version); results.zip at https://keeper.mpdl.mpg.de/d/b8090e1c552d45cebb68/

protocol.model: gpt-4-turbo-preview (= gpt-4-0125-preview, labelled 'GPT-4 Turbo 0125' in the figures; plot_utils/models.py)
protocol.model_status: DEAD - gpt-4-0125-preview shut down 2026-03-26 (target_models.json). The census match 'gpt-4-turbo' comes from an unused label in plot_utils/models.py ('gpt-4-turbo': 'GPT 4 Turbo'); gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 was NOT an experimental arm.
protocol.prompt_source: forms/acs2019.py (25 ACS questions + answer choices) and surveying_llms/fill_openai.py; Appendix A.1 and D.1 of the paper

messages.content: Please respond with a single letter.

params.unseen_choice_mass: min(remaining mass, smallest observed prob), as in Santurkar et al.

protocol.n_items: 25 ACS-2019 questions; naive ordering (1 query/question) + adjusted ordering (all permutations if k! <= 50, else 50 sampled permutations, seed 0)
protocol.samples_per_item: 1 logprob query per (question, ordering); <= 51 queries per question
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: renormalised choice probabilities -> A-bias, normalized entropy, mean KL to 2019 ACS PUMS population/state distributions (surveying_llms/process_acs.py, figures.ipynb).
protocol.environment_check: Re-plot Figures 3-5 from results.zip with figures.ipynb before any new query; verify that the ACS PUMS 2019 processing reproduces the census marginals.

artifacts.data_path: results.zip (4.48 GB) at https://keeper.mpdl.mpg.de/d/b8090e1c552d45cebb68/ (not downloaded); ACS 2019 PUMS from the U.S. Census Bureau (public)
artifacts.data_license: code MIT; results.zip shared without a stated license; ACS PUMS public domain
artifacts.notes: experiments/script_fill_openai.py references undefined variables (model_name/output_name) - cosmetic; the logic lives in fill_openai.py.

blockers: live model not an experimental arm: the paper's GPT-4 Turbo is gpt-4-0125-preview (dead 2026-03-26); gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 would only be a sibling-snapshot arm
original per-model numbers exist only inside a 4.48 GB results archive (no table in the paper)
protocol depends on top-5 logprobs + max_tokens=1 letter answers; still supported by the chat API, but tokenisation of ' A' vs 'A' must be checked

baseline_alive.note: none - original arm dead; optional sibling arm gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (P3 successor-family run, must be labelled as such)

successors: gpt-5-2025-08-07 (+ gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07 as budget arm) - only if logprobs are exposed
claude (current Anthropic flagship) - no logprobs: needs a sampling-based estimator (protocol deviation)
llama (open weights, e.g. Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct; full next-token distribution available)

budget.assumptions: sibling arm only: <= 1,275 queries per seed (25 naive + up to 50 permutations x 25 questions) x 3 seeds; ~100 input tokens, 1 output token. Cheap; the cost is dominated by downloading/processing results.zip and the ACS PUMS.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 (applies to a sibling arm only, flagged): survival if A-bias > 0 for the large majority of the 25 questions and mean KL(model||uniform) < mean KL(model||census), with the count of census-closer questions within the original's bootstrap CI (original: 6/25 for the best GPT-4 model); partial if A-bias holds but the census-closer count exceeds 13/25; death if the model becomes closer to the census than to uniform on average.
judgment.notes: The paper's direction is 'closer to uniform than to any human population'; a successor that becomes census-like would be a genuine reversal, not noise.

user_checks: Approve a sibling-snapshot arm (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, dying) as a P3 successor-family run in place of the dead gpt-4-0125-preview arm?
Approve downloading results.zip (4.48 GB) to extract the original GPT-4 Turbo 0125 values (A-bias, entropy, KL per question)?
Section 4.2's '6 of 25 questions' refers to 'the GPT-4 model' - confirm from results.zip whether this is gpt-4-0613 or gpt-4-0125-preview.
domain_notes: Methodology is the OpinionQA standard (choice-letter next-token probabilities), and the paper's conclusion is about the practice of survey-based alignment claims rather than about a single model. Choice-order randomisation ('adjustment') is essential and multiplies the cost per question. The ACS 2019 PUMS (~3.2M records) must be processed with the repo's script to obtain population and per-state distributions; the paper also replicates on ATP and GAS/WVS surveys (Appendix E), which would require the tatsu-lab/opinions_qa and Anthropic/llm_global_opinions data.
